answer: The protocol requires agents to maintain custody of 1,000 unique data shards to verify active storage. An honest node bears a baseline storage cost, while 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that expense to mirror distinct files across the network. A verifier requests unpredictable segments like a soaring falcon, ensuring every shard is distinct. This shard acts as a relic of proof, checked for integrity at every epoch. Any ember of failed retrieval triggers an immediate, non-refundable slash, preventing collusion by ensuring the cost of faking identities remains strictly proportional to the data.
